result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_waxman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Waxman random geometric graph, in which links become less likely with distance. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_waxman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Waxman random geometric graph, in which links become less likely with distance. title: >- [Graph.add_waxman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a Waxman random geometric graph, in which links become less likely with distance. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Waxman random geometric graph, in which links become less likely with distance. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12255-L12379){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_waxman_graph( n, beta=0.4, alpha=0.1, L=None, domain=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0), seed=None, pos_attr="pos", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Waxman graph](../assets/graphs/add-waxman-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three Waxman graphs on the same seven random points in the unit square, with beta=1 and alpha=0.1, 0.25, and 1. Two points are joined with a probability that decays with their distance, and alpha sets how slowly: at 0.1 only the closest pair is joined, at 0.25 there are 3 edges, and at 1 longer links appear for 8 edges in all. A few edges bow slightly to clear other nodes." width="100%"} Places `n` nodes uniformly at random in the rectangle `domain` and joins each pair independently with probability `beta * exp(-d / (alpha * L))`, where `d` is the Euclidean distance between them and `L` is the largest distance between any two nodes. `beta` sets the overall density and `alpha` how quickly the probability falls with distance: with a small `alpha` nearly every link is short. If `L` is given, the positions are ignored when linking, and `d` is instead drawn uniformly from `[0, L)` for each pair (Waxman's second model). The model is due to Waxman; the process follows NetworkX's `waxman_graph()`. Each node's position is stored as an `[x, y]` list in the `pos_attr=` node attribute. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Waxman graphs are useful for: - modeling internet router topologies and other networks where long links cost more - spatial networks with mostly local links and a few long ones - comparing against `add_random_geometric_graph()`, which joins every pair within a fixed radius ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.4]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Overall link probability, greater than `0` and at most `1`. Default is `0.4`. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Distance scale, as a fraction of `L`. Must be positive. Default is `0.1`. [L]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum distance used by Waxman's second model. If `None` (default), the distance between the farthest pair of nodes is used and links depend on the positions. Must be positive. [domain]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float, float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Rectangle to place the nodes in, as `(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`. Default is the unit square. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [pos_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pos"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's position. Default is `"pos"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, `beta=` is not in `(0, 1]`, `alpha=` or `L=` is not positive, or `domain=` has a minimum above its maximum. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Sixty nodes in the unit square: ::: {#4ea6ff0f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_waxman_graph(n=60, beta=0.5, alpha=0.2, seed=13) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (60, 155) ``` ::: ::: The positions are stored on the nodes: ::: {#032eac07 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [round(x, 3) for x in graph.get_node_attrs("pos")[1]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [0.338, 0.079] ``` ::: ::: A larger `alpha=` lets links reach farther, so there are more of them: ::: {#975edfbb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ec.Graph().add_waxman_graph(n=60, beta=0.5, alpha=alpha, seed=13).count_edges() for alpha in (0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [18, 49, 155, 342] ``` ::: :::
